newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr in thin volume trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr in thin volume trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed New Year day on Wednesday at 35.845/855 against the dollar, up from the opening rate of 35.87/89 rupees, dealers said.
Dollar sales by a leading Calcutta-based bank soon after the market opened in the morning and poor demand for dollars determined the day's trend, dealers said.
"The volumes were very thin," said a dealer.
"The rupee regained from its fiscal low of 35.96 to 35.87 as Friday play dominated," said a foreign bank in a forex commentary, referring to Friday value spot deals.
Forward dollar premia continued to ease on Wednesday on expectations of improved liquidity following a 50 basis point cut planned by the Reserve Bank of India on January 4.
